title: Eastern Hemlock: Ancient Hemlocks You Can Visit
meta_description: A slow conifer of the Appalachian and Great Lakes forests. Philadelphia's weeping hemlock was a sensation at the 1876 Centennial Exposition.
intro: The eastern hemlock is a slow-growing conifer of the Appalachian and Great Lakes forests. At Morris Arboretum in Philadelphia, a weeping hemlock came from the 1876 Centennial Exposition, where the weeping form caused a sensation among horticulturists; it was dug up and moved to the Meadowbrook Avenue gate in 1947, and its twin by the pond fell in a snowstorm in February 2024. In Minneapolis, at the far western edge of the range, Eloise Butler planted hemlocks by hand in 1911 and 1914, and the biggest of them is now a state co-champion of a species Minnesota lists as Endangered. Delaware's second-largest grows in Brandywine Cemetery in Wilmington, 2.59 metres round and 25.6 metres tall, though nobody has posted a dated sighting of it in recent years.
